decisive_items: sustained a dog bite on her right thumb approximately one week before admission
Gram stain showed thin, fusiform gram-negative rods in two of four bottles
response.rationale: R3 uniquely links the dog bite exposure to fusiform gram-negative rods on blood culture and the systemic inflammatory response, making Capnocytophaga canimorsus sepsis the most specific supported diagnosis. R4 identifies the organism but omits sepsis; R1 captures sepsis but not the organism; R2/R5 are unsupported by absent schistocytes and normal haptoglobin/fibrinogen; R6 is unsupported by imaging and clinical context.

rejected.why: Thrombocytopenia and petechiae are present, but normal haptoglobin/fibrinogen and no schistocytes argue against DIC; blood cultures point to infection.
No schistocytes and normal haptoglobin make TTP unlikely; culture-proven infection better explains the thrombocytopenia.
Sepsis syndrome is present, but this candidate lacks the specific organism identified by dog bite and blood culture.
GI bleeding is not supported by imaging or a bleeding source; low iron and macrocytosis are nonspecific and infection explains the presentation.
Correct organism, but it fails to capture the concurrent sepsis syndrome that R3 explicitly includes.
